answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because nectar only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. In practice marble is enforced by the ledger itself: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any cedar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
